themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints surged to 35 this week versus an 8-week average of 8.4 per week—a 318% spike (z-score: 8.88)—suggesting either a new contamination discovery, water system issue, or increased awareness in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens this week.
evidence: 35 lead complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (318% increase)
Z-score of 8.88 indicates statistically severe anomaly
Aligns with ongoing community board budget request to inspect water mains and repair/replace as needed
reporting_angles: Which water main segments or buildings are affected? Interview NYC DEP and affected residents about the source
Is this tied to the active 46 Nelson Street Rezoning or other construction that may have disturbed old pipes?

themes_detail.label: Bus shelter infrastructure crisis
themes_detail.summary: Bus Stop Shelter complaints exploded to 5 this week from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3900% spike (z-score: 14.74)—indicating rapid deterioration of transit infrastructure in the district this week.
evidence: 5 bus shelter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3900% spike, z-score: 14.74)
Highest z-score among all spikes in the dataset, indicating most statistically dramatic anomaly
No prior sustained complaints about shelters—suggests a sudden, localized event or failure
reporting_angles: Which bus stops are affected and what is the damage? Interview MTA about repair timeline
Tie to broader transit equity concerns in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens alongside heat/hot water complaints

themes_detail.label: Overgrown trees threatening safety
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown Tree/Branches complaints jumped to 21 this week from a 3.5-per-week baseline—a 500% spike (z-score: 8.03)—suggesting either recent storm damage, deferred maintenance, or seasonal growth acceleration in the district this week.
evidence: 21 overgrown tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 8.03)
Related spike: 3 New Tree Requests this week vs. 0.4 baseline (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)—residents both reporting hazards and requesting replanting
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for park reconstruction and tree maintenance
reporting_angles: Did recent weather (high winds, storms) trigger branch falls? Check NWS records and NYC Parks incident reports
Interview Parks Dept on backlog: are crews overwhelmed, or is this deferred maintenance coming due?

themes_detail.label: Asbestos hazard uptick
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints reached 4 this week from a 0.6-per-week baseline—a 540% spike (z-score: 4.85)—pointing to either discovery of contamination in older buildings or new construction disturbance of known hazards this week.
evidence: 4 asbestos complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 4.85)
Correlates with 155 new building filings and 824 alteration filings in last 90 days—renovation/demolition activity may be exposing asbestos
Historic housing stock in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens (pre-1980s construction) at high risk
reporting_angles: Which buildings are triggering complaints? Cross-reference with DOB permits to identify construction sites disturbing asbestos
Are contractors and building owners following proper abatement protocols? Interview NYC DOH enforcement

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints escalating
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Park complaints spiked to 5 last week from a 0.4-per-week baseline—a 1233% increase (z-score: 9.55)—indicating a new or intensifying disturbance source in a neighborhood park last week.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (1233% spike, z-score: 9.55)
Distinct from general residential noise (573 complaints over 90 days)—suggests localized park issue
Aligns with CB budget request for enhanced park safety and enforcement staff
reporting_angles: Which park? Prospect Park or smaller neighborhood green spaces? Interview Parks Enforcement and residents on what the noise source is
Is this event-based (permitted events, concerts) or ongoing (construction, street noise)?
